A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Renumbered tables and reorganized proofs can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments measuring perplexity, downstream accuracy, variance, and layer effectiveness across depth, weight decay, sequence length, GQA, and MoE configurations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds usefulness-threshold sensitivity and initialization comparisons in Appendices A.8–A.9.

M1.justification: The Transformer components, sparsity mechanisms, MoE routing, and combined training recipe remain unchanged. The MoE scaling derivation is retained under reorganized appendix headings; the new initialization experiment is a comparison, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu for training and held-out evaluation, with MMLU, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and HellaSwag downstream evaluations. The new appendix analyses reuse existing task coverage, depths, and context lengths.

E2.justification: Appendix A.9 newly evaluates Zhang et al. (2019) scaled initialization against normal initialization in Table 7. v1 discussed scaled initialization as prior work without reporting this comparison. Existing dense/MoE and attention comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new A.8 evaluation varies the usefulness threshold over 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 for depths 16/32 and sequence lengths 1024/4096. A.9 adds initialization treatments for a 16-layer model. Previously stated main-experiment budgets and metric definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: A.8 adds a focused check of whether usefulness rankings depend on the chosen threshold. A.9 tests whether longer-context benefits persist with scaled initialization. Existing variance, kurtosis, entropy, and layer-intervention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains its statement that results are averaged over three random seeds, and existing error-bar reporting is unchanged. The added appendix tables introduce no run-count disclosures, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 1 and Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results. New Tables 6–7 add sensitivity and initialization outcomes; for example, L=16, T=1024 has usefulness 0.88/0.75/0.63 at thresholds 0.05/0.1/0.2. Causal-effect heatmaps in Figures 20–29 also change, including reduced final-column dominance in several panels. The PDFs do not explain the origin of these plot revisions.

T1.justification: v2 removes the complete GQA/MQA variance theorem and proof from v1 Appendix B.6, including Theorem 5 and Equations 78–89, withdrawing formal support for one central mechanism. Section 2 also removes the claim that Weierstrass guarantees convergence from the bounded Jacobian norm. Other principal bounds remain; the MoE theorem and norm derivation are retained and reorganized.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the causal claim that sparsity improves depth utilization, instead describing evidence that sparsity-like mechanisms are associated with better utilization. The introduction broadens the stated meaning of sparsity. The central experimental contributions, practical recipe, and conclusion otherwise remain largely unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section and appendix qualifications substantially restrict the theory's applicability: independent masks, uniform attention or gating, and uncoupled experts are idealizations rather than predictive descriptions of trained Transformers. Sections 2 and 4.2.1 replace causal interpretations with associations. These changes materially clarify the boundary between the mathematical models and empirical evidence.

D1.justification: A.9 newly discloses normal initialization with mean 0 and standard deviation 0.02 for all linear layers and identifies the scaled-initialization reference. This documents the existing default rather than establishing that it changed. Framework, tokenizer, hardware, optimizer, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds three Ma et al. quantization references and Zheng et al. (2025) on network pruning. A.9 also examines complementarity with previously cited scaled initialization. The main related-work organization and positioning around sparsity and variance control remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and selected explanatory passages, adds Limitations and Impact Statement sections, updates the publication footer, and reorganizes appendix headings and equation numbering. Most prose and the overall narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–7, retains the earlier configuration tables as Tables 8–10, redraws and rescales causal-effect panels in Figures 20–29, and relocates Figures 7–8. Most figures, table structures, and the overall layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added threshold and initialization checks strengthen specific aspects of the empirical support. Explicit theory limitations and removal of the unjustified convergence guarantee improve claim calibration. The gain is limited: the main evidence is unchanged, no replacement GQA proof is supplied, causal-heatmap revisions remain unexplained, and the conclusion retains stronger language than the revised qualifications.
